properties.title: Reliable machine learning models in genomic medicine using conformal prediction

properties.name: TCP/ICP post-hoc genomic prediction-set/interval component
properties.scope_limits: Three task-specific fitted models, not one reusable world-state representation.

scope.population: Retrospective genomic patient cohorts and cancer cell lines; three separate use cases
scope.time_horizon: Static molecular/subtype/drug-response prediction; no health-world transition

assertions.applicability_reason: Supporting static genomic SVM/XGBoost/RF prediction-set/interval methods have no propagated health-world state or action transition, forecast rollout, causal-treatment contrast, model-based planner or agent. Response outcomes under a drug are labels/readouts rather than settable simulated clinical actions;72hassay endpoint is not temporal dynamics.

legacy_cells.B: Reliable machine learning models in genomic medicine using conformal prediction
legacy_cells.C: Christina Papangelou, Konstantinos Kyriakidis, Pantelis Natsiavas, Ioanna Chouvarda, Andigoni Malousi
legacy_cells.I: 032_2024_Reliable machine learning models in genomic medicine using conformal prediction.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Rheumatoid arthritis; Crohn’s disease; diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; cancer-cell-line response to afatinib
legacy_cells.S: Whether conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty and flags unreliable genomic predictions of infliximab response and DLBCL subtype, and provides prediction intervals for afatinib IC50.
legacy_cells.T: 44 Crohn’s disease patients and 34 rheumatoid arthritis patients; 1,311 DLBCL samples (including 278 unclassified); 765 cancer cell lines, reduced to 677 after preprocessing.
legacy_cells.V: Flag uncertain predictions for expert review rather than making definitive assignments in ambiguous cases.
legacy_cells.CR: Empirical coverage evaluated: 93.75% (binary TCP); 95.20% (DLBCL ICP test); 96.6% (external DLBCL cohort); 92.6% (afatinib regression at significance level 0.90).
legacy_cells.DN: GEO GSE42296; GEO GSE181063; Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC); GEO GSE117556 (external DLBCL cohort)
legacy_cells.DQ: 44 Crohn’s disease patients; 34 rheumatoid arthritis patients; 1,311 DLBCL samples (345 ABC, 517 GCB, 170 MHG, 278 unclassified); external DLBCL cohort 789 samples; 765 cancer cell lines, reduced to 677 after preprocessing.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors evaluate conformal-prediction approaches in three genomic-medicine applications: binary infliximab response prediction, DLBCL subtype classification under distribution shift, and afatinib response regression.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results include 87% accuracy (AUC=0.9) for the binary SVM; 4.8% error for conformalized DLBCL test classification versus 16.25% for XGBoost alone; 96.6% empirical coverage on an external DLBCL dataset; and 92.6% coverage for afatinib regression at 0.90 significance.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors note that conformal prediction provides marginal rather than per-instance or subgroup conditional coverage; distribution shifts, class imbalance, and limited availability of representative or rare calibration data remain challenges.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors state that in-depth research and practical applications are needed to address challenges and realize uncertainty-informed multi-omics use in clinical environments.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that conformal prediction has not been sufficiently used in joint applications of genomics and medicine.
legacy_cells.FR: The experiments are static response/subtype/IC50 prediction with conformal uncertainty and empirical coverage. They do not demonstrate persistent patient state, temporal transitions or rollouts, action-conditioned dynamics, identified treatment effects, planning/control, or prospective clinical benefit.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M7 Outcome & causal layer; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Reuse the evaluated supporting estimator or audit behind a clear component boundary; validate its uncertainty and task limits again when connected to temporal dynamics.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–34: title/abstract and Introduction (pp. 1–15); Experimental setting, all three application methods and Results (pp. 16–22), including Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–4 captions; Discussion and stated limitations/future-work implications (pp. 23–25); data/code availability and references (pp. 26–34).
